title: Directive and Pipe Testing knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Directive and Pipe Testing”?
options: Directive and Pipe Testing means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Directive and Pipe Testing removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Directive and Pipe Testing should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Directive and Pipe Testing helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.answer_key: Directive and Pipe Testing helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Directive and Pipe Testing is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Testing a directive on a host element” in this lesson?
options: Assume “Testing a directive on a host element” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Testing a directive on a host element” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Testing a directive on a host element” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Testing a directive on a host element” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Testing a directive on a host element” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Testing a directive on a host element” under Directive and Pipe Testing. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Directive and Pipe Testing”?
options: Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
